text:
Sean Gallagher: We’ve now had a couple “demo tenant is slow/broken” moments in front of Sales. We need to stop handling this ad hoc.

Proposal: define (1) a lightweight oncall/escalation path for demo outages, and (2) an acceptable error budget / SLO for the demo tenant (business hours only). Can we align today so we can wire alerts + runbook updates this week?

Rafael Mendes: +1. Right now it’s basically “ping random people in Slack”. Not great when someone is 10 min from a prospect call.

Talia Benson: adding here from program mgmt side — CRO is asking for a clear owner + what “good” looks like (metrics) for Standard Demo v1.

Markus Klein: from field POV: I don’t need 24/7, I need: if the tenant is degraded within ~1 hour of a scheduled demo, there’s a deterministic playbook + someone to page.

Priya Natarajan: agree on not making this a huge operational burden, but we should define the boundary. Also: SRE shouldn’t be the only stop — some fixes are routing/pool-level.

Sean Gallagher: exactly. Let’s define “demo-impacting” first.

My strawman:
- Demo-impacting = any of:
  1) API 5xx > 1% over 5m for `demo-std-v1`
  2) p95 end-to-end latency > 3s over 10m for the core routes (chat/embeddings)
  3) p95 TTFB (streaming) > 2s over 10m
  4) sustained throttling (429) > 0.5% over 10m (usually quota misconfig)
- Console/dashboard lag is annoying, but not an “outage” unless traces/requests are also missing.

Thoughts?

Logan Wright: thresholds look reasonable. I’d tweak wording so Sales doesn’t chase noisy 5m windows. For latency, make it “p95 > 3s AND request volume > N” so a single slow request doesn’t trip.

Chloe Martin: +1. Also can we treat “Console saved view 500s / blank panels” as its own severity? People use it live as proof. If the UI is down, the demo is functionally impacted.

Sean Gallagher: fair. Maybe classify:
- Sev2 (demo blocked): API errors or core route unusable
- Sev3 (demo degraded): UI/Console issues OR latency above target but still usable

Mina Haddad: +1 on severity split. Also for routing issues: if primary pool saturates, our first-line action should be flipping the pre-approved failover policy for demo routes (primary -> secondary). That’s safer than “debug” mid-demo.

Rafael Mendes: ok, so oncall path should encode “route around, then investigate”.

Cole Summers: 429s are *usually* on us (quota defaults / someone ran load tests on demo tenant). We can add an alert on 429 rate and auto-post the top offender key in #eng-sre so we can revoke quickly.

Markus Klein: please yes. Also: who’s allowed to flip failover? In the sales thread last week we did it quickly, but I don’t want random folks editing tenant config.

Priya Natarajan: permissions-wise, we can keep “config change” to a small set (SRE + platform oncall). SEs should have view-only + run scripts.

Talia Benson: can we document that explicitly in the runbook? (who can change routes, who can change quotas, etc.)

Rafael Mendes: yup.

Sean Gallagher: oncall path proposal (lightweight):

Coverage window:
- Mon–Fri
- 08:00–18:00 local time per region (NA + EMEA)
- Outside that, “best effort” (no paging), and SEs should default to Plan B (deck/screenshots).

Escalation:
1) SE/AEs post in #demo-tenant-help (or #sales) with :rotating_light: + include:
   - time of demo
   - tenant (`demo-std-v1`)
   - route name
   - symptom (slow/5xx/429/UI)
   - dashboard link (Grafana overview)
2) RedwoodBot auto-forward to #eng-sre with tag `demo-tenant` and page “Demo Tenant Oncall” if within coverage window.
3) Demo Tenant Oncall = Primary: SRE (Rafael) / Secondary: Platform (Priya) (or the inverse, but one named primary).
4) First action is always one of:
   a) apply failover routing policy for demo core routes
   b) bump min replicas for demo pool (if saturation)
   c) quick quota reset/revoke offending key (if 429)
5) If not mitigated in 10 min, open an incident bridge (Slack huddle) + post Plan B instructions back to Sales.

Does that seem workable?

Rafael Mendes: workable. I’d rather not introduce a brand new channel, though. Could we standardize on #eng-sre + tag `demo-tenant` + Sales can still ping, but bot tells them what to include?

Markus Klein: I’m fine either way. The main thing is: a clear template so people don’t just say “it’s slow”.

RedwoodBot: :information_source: Suggestion: create a saved Slack workflow “Report demo tenant issue” to collect required fields (tenant, route, region, dashboard link, minutes to demo) and post to #eng-sre with tag `demo-tenant`.

Talia Benson: workflow sounds good + aligns with “single source of truth”.

Sean Gallagher: cool. On error budget / SLO: we need something we can measure that isn’t insane.

Option A (SLO):
- Availability SLO (business-hours): 99.5% for core demo routes (chat + embeddings) measured by synthetic checks.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 2.5s, TTFB p95 < 1.5s during business-hours.

Option B (incident budget):
- Max 2 demo-impacting incidents per month during business-hours.

I prefer A because it’s objective, but 99.5% might be aggressive for a demo tenant unless we reserve capacity.

Priya Natarajan: 99.5% business-hours is OK if we treat demo tenant like “semi-prod”: pinned versions, reserved min replicas, failover pool with headroom.

Logan Wright: measuring availability by synthetic is easy. We can run a canary every 60s on:
- `/v1/chat.completions` (streaming off + on)
- `/v1/embeddings`
And publish “demo-std-v1 canary pass rate” dashboard + alert.

Chloe Martin: +1. Also add a lightweight Console synthetic (hit the saved view endpoint) if we can, but don’t page on that unless API is also failing.

Cole Summers: if we do 99.5% availability, that’s ~18 min downtime per 5 business days (assuming ~50 hours). That feels tight but doable if failover is our immediate mitigation.

Rafael Mendes: practical question: do we want pages for “degraded but not down”? If we page on every p95 blip we’ll get alert fatigue.

Sean Gallagher: agree. Let’s page only on Sev2 (“blocked”) conditions. Sev3 (“degraded”) posts to channel + creates a ticket, no page.

Mina Haddad: define Sev2 as:
- 5xx > 1% (5m) OR canary failing 3 consecutive runs
- OR p95 TTFB > 2s for 10m AND qps > 0.5
Then paging is justified.

Markus Klein: can we also add “within 60 min of a scheduled demo” as a page boost? Like, if it’s degraded at 9pm maybe no one cares, but if it’s 15 min before a demo it’s existential.

Talia Benson: we do have the calendar of scheduled demo trainings/dry runs, but not prospect demos. AEs don’t always log them.

Rafael Mendes: I’d rather not rely on calendars. But the workflow could include “minutes to demo” and we treat <60m as “page even if Sev3”.

Sean Gallagher: that’s a good compromise.

Proposed policy:
- Default paging: Sev2 only, during coverage window.
- Override: if workflow says “minutes to demo <= 60”, page on Sev3 as well.

Priya Natarajan: ok. Ownership: SRE owns alerts/oncall process + first mitigation; platform owns capacity/autoscaler fixes; routing team owns failover policies correctness.

Rafael Mendes: action items I’ll take:
1) Draft “Demo Tenant Oncall Policy” section for the runbook (coverage, severity, paging criteria, who can flip failover)
2) Add Grafana alerts:
   - demo canary failures
   - 5xx rate
   - sustained queue depth / replicas < desired
   - 429 rate
3) Set up Slack workflow (with RedwoodBot help) to collect required info

Need inputs:
- @Mina Haddad confirm the exact failover policy name + steps (so we can put it as step 1)
- @Logan Wright provide canary endpoints + expected success criteria

Mina Haddad: failover policy is `demo-chat-failover-v1` (applies to routes `chat-demo-primary` + `chat-demo-tools`). Steps are basically “apply policy preset” in Console -> Routing -> Policies. I’ll send screenshots + exact clickpath.

Logan Wright: will post a snippet for the synthetic checks. We can do it from the existing canary runner. Success criteria: HTTP 200 + token stream starts within 1.5s for streaming check.

Chloe Martin: I’ll add a “Demo Live” saved view preset (1h window, p95, canary status, queue depth) so the first responder isn’t hunting panels.

Markus Klein: and I’ll update SE enablement: when this happens, do not freestyle; use Plan B (mini hosted API + screenshots) if mitigation isn’t immediate.

Sean Gallagher: great. Let’s target having the paging + workflow live by end of week. If we can hit 99.5% business-hours for 30 days, we can call it “stable” for v1.

Talia Benson: I’ll track these in the demo env program board and send an update to Jordan/Markus/Soojin once we have the policy text.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: I’ll post the draft in #eng-sre tomorrow for review.
